title: Credit metrics
objectives: Answer out loud: Calculate leverage and coverage.
Answer out loud: What do lenders focus on?

steps.heading: Leverage
steps.body: Total debt ÷ EBITDA; Net debt ÷ EBITDA. How many years of EBITDA to repay debt.

steps.heading: Coverage
steps.body: EBITDA ÷ interest; (EBITDA − CapEx) ÷ interest. Can the company afford its interest?

steps.heading: Cash flow
steps.body: FCF ÷ debt. How fast can it pay down debt?
Typical LBO leverage: roughly 4–6x EBITDA, depending on the business and credit markets.

legend.meaning: Years of EBITDA to repay debt — lower is safer
How many times EBITDA covers interest — higher is safer

blocks.template: Higher leverage ratios mean {{1}} credit risk

blocks.title: Why is (EBITDA − CapEx) ÷ interest more conservative than EBITDA ÷ interest?
blocks.teaser: CapEx is a real cash need.
blocks.body: CapEx is a real cash need. A capital-intensive company might cover interest easily on EBITDA but barely after funding CapEx.

blocks.prompt: EBITDA $100, CapEx $40, interest $25. What's (EBITDA − CapEx) ÷ interest?
blocks.explanation: ($100 − $40) ÷ $25 = 2.4x. On EBITDA alone it would look like 4.0x — CapEx is a real cash need, so this ratio is more conservative.

blocks.title: Gross vs. net leverage?
blocks.teaser: Net leverage subtracts cash, reflecting debt the company couldn't repay immediately.
blocks.body: Net leverage subtracts cash, reflecting debt the company couldn't repay immediately. Lenders often focus on gross leverage, since cash can be spent.

blocks.title: What do lenders care about most?
blocks.teaser: Getting repaid: stable cash flow, coverage, collateral, and covenants.
blocks.body:
Getting repaid: stable cash flow, coverage, collateral, and covenants. They don't share in the upside, so they focus on downside protection.

**Interview answer:** "Lenders don't get the upside, so they care about downside — cash flow stability, coverage, and collateral."
